title: Accept a TCP connection
summary: Open a listening TCP socket with correct byte order and checked system calls.

scenario.briefing: A campus device reports telemetry over TCP. The listener assigns a host-order port and ignores bind failures. Repair the setup so the service binds all interfaces and reports failure.

objectives.description: Create a listening socket with the correct port byte order.
Order the TCP server calls correctly.
Explain sockets, byte order, and accept accurately.

hints: Convert the port before assigning it to sin_port.
Check every system call that can return -1.
Close the descriptor when bind or listen fails.
Use htons((uint16_t)port) and return the listener only after listen succeeds.

misconceptions.description: Assigning a host-order port to sin_port.
misconceptions.testDescription: The port is converted to network byte order.
misconceptions.feedback: sin_port uses network byte order. Assign htons((uint16_t)port) so the server listens on the intended port.
A socket must be bound before it can listen. The order is socket, bind, listen, accept.

misconceptions.description: Believing accept reuses the listening socket for the connection.
misconceptions.feedback: accept returns a new descriptor for the connection. The listening socket remains open for other clients.

sections.title: A listening socket has an order
sections.body: A TCP server creates a socket, binds it to an address and port, listens for connections, and accepts one connection at a time. The socket returned by accept is a new descriptor for that connection; the listening socket stays open for later clients.

sections.title: Byte order is part of the wire format
sections.body: Network protocols use big-endian byte order. htons converts a 16-bit port from host order to network order, and htonl does the same for 32-bit values. Assigning a host-order port directly produces a server that listens on the wrong port.

sections.title: Check every system call
sections.body: socket, bind, listen, and accept return -1 on failure and set errno. Close the descriptor on a failed bind or listen so the process does not leak it. A server that ignores errors looks alive while serving nothing.

steps.title: Open the listener
steps.prompt: Edit main.c. open_listener creates a TCP socket, enables address reuse, binds INADDR_ANY on the supplied port, and listens with a backlog of 8.

localVerification.description: Compile main.c with a POSIX C toolchain (Linux, macOS, or WSL); the socket headers are POSIX, not native Windows.

tests.description: The port is converted to network byte order.
Socket creation is checked before use.
The listener binds all interfaces and listens.

hints: The port currently goes into sin_port unchanged.
A failed socket call returns a negative descriptor.
Close the listener if bind or listen fails.

steps.title: Order the server calls
steps.prompt: A TCP server must accept one connection. Which call order is correct?

quiz.explanation: The socket exists first, bind attaches the address, listen marks it ready, and accept returns a connection descriptor.

hints: The socket must exist before it can be bound.

steps.explanation: Network order is part of the protocol, accept returns a new descriptor, and bind must precede listen. The listening socket remains available.
hints: The listening socket is not the connection socket.
